correctness.rationale: For every m>=3, the closed-cell deleted product is a natural finite homology model. The established Lütgehetmann–Recio-Mitter Proposition 5.4 proves connected graph homotopy type, implying H_1 free abelian and H_k=0 for k>=2. Explicit cell counts give chi=2+m-m^2 and b1=m^2-m-1. Four exactly counted signed chain-trace cases give the full formula for all group elements. The signed ordered-pair quotient matches the complete character, hence the rational representation in characteristic zero. Pole reversal has the negative-rank trace, so its order-two action is -I rationally and then on the free integral lattice. Both actual standalone verification programs independently check all 3,480 actions for m=3,...,6, all cubical boundary squares and chain-equivariance, and boundary ranks modulo 2,3,5 for m=3,...,7. Finite runs are checks, not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest prior papers, Barnett–Farber 2009 and Lütgehetmann–Recio-Mitter 2018, cover the identical homology model and graph-homotopy type but not its full S_m × C2 × C2 symmetry character, rational quotient model, or integral negative pole action. value.rationale: All m>=3 are treated in a canonical non-tree graph family with two high-valence poles; two labeled particles supply the first natural collision-sensitive case. The full arm, pole, and particle interplay resolves two distinct Z/2 actions and yields a structural rational permutation quotient and an integral nontrivial scalar-action constraint. These are not recoverable from previously known Betti numbers or graph homotopy equivalence; the all-parameter classification is reusable for equivariant graph-configuration topology.
